scope.context: The repository had substantial pre-existing uncommitted changes and a concurrent user task. Both were preserved. Findings describe observed original vulnerabilities; extensions identify fixed-in-worktree status. No commit, push, hosted migration or deployment was performed.
limitations: Single-pass repository security review, not exhaustive formal verification or live penetration testing.
No target hosted Auth/Storage/infrastructure or existing production data validation.
TAC authorization connector not signed in (USER_NOT_LOGGED_IN).
Two moderate tooling-only dependency paths remain documented; web runtime audit has zero alerts.
Some test bodies executed without exhaustive manual inspection.
Concurrent source changes after the verified snapshot require fresh validation.
scope.runtimeStatus: Local build/typecheck/lint/tests and browser smoke pass; target hosted runtime and native hardware unverified.
scope.summary: Full repository single-pass Codex Security review with independent core, offline, supplemental and UI source inspections; seven validated security findings fixed in the working tree, plus production correctness and dependency remediation.
scope.validationMode: Source validation and local isolated execution with synthetic service configuration, PGlite, fake IndexedDB, disposable PostgreSQL and built HTTP app.

threatModel.summary: MINIROS is a multi-business retail operations web/PWA: browser inputs enter Next App Router Server Actions or offline Route Handlers, use server authorization and shared contracts/domain code, then commit Drizzle transactions to Supabase Postgres; Supabase supplies Auth, Storage and Realtime. Owners/admins manage shifts/configuration/recovery and employees operate assigned shifts/POS/production. Production root start launches @miniros/web next start; package build additionally emits PWA assets. Astro marketing is separate; API workflow-preview and agent/mobile shells are supporting scaffolds, not the new offline authority path. This architecture review covers the current source state and supporting controls, not completed vulnerability coverage. Sources: README.md:3-20; docs/architecture.md:9-26; package.json:7-16; apps/web/package.json:5-8; apps/api/src/server.ts:12-59.
trustBoundaries: Browser to Next service: client-supplied business cookie and operation inputs are not authorization. requireUser verifies Supabase identity; requireActiveBusiness verifies active membership/business, role, feature, POS/production capability and assigned shift. Actions parse Zod contracts; offline JSON POSTs additionally enforce Origin and streamed 1,000,000-byte input limit. Sources: apps/web/src/server/services/access.ts:30-199; apps/web/src/server/actions/operations.ts:62-79; apps/web/src/server/services/offline-http.ts:5-14; apps/web/src/server/services/offline-http.ts:47-83.

Ordinary employee versus administrator: admin shift wrappers derive actor server-side with admin=true; creation/update/bulk run transactional workflows with business-schedule lock. Recovery freeze/restore/journal require same-business admin access and record reason/audit. Sources: apps/web/src/server/services/admin-shifts.ts:54-78; apps/web/src/server/services/schedule-lock.ts:8-14; apps/web/src/server/services/offline-admin.ts:84-135; apps/web/src/server/services/offline-admin.ts:186-206.

Prepared device versus ordinary writer: cookie hash + storage UUID + current authenticated user/business/assignment + session/snapshot identity are checked by server, rather than accepting browser catalogue authority. Row locks and unique active-owner constraint serialize reservation; nonprepared operations call assertUnreservedShift. Sources: apps/web/src/server/services/offline-prepare.ts:24-114; apps/web/src/server/services/offline-sync.ts:41-74; apps/web/src/server/services/offline-context.ts:31-71; supabase/migrations/20260905040950_offline_shift_sessions.sql:48-58.

Untrusted offline envelope to durable business effects: canonical digest binds original payload to action ID/session; expected sequence/clock/state checked, server snapshot supplies prepared context, domain work uses nested transaction, journal/result and acknowledged sequence committed together. Sources: apps/web/src/server/services/offline-sync.ts:28-50; apps/web/src/server/services/offline-sync.ts:75-175; apps/web/src/server/services/offline-sync.ts:335-441.

Browser Supabase API versus server DB/Storage authority: TypeScript Pick restricts normal local callers but does not authorize remote requests; SQL grants/RLS and server role credentials are the actual independently enforced interfaces. Authenticated Data API retains SELECT on business tables and journal; session/pilot tables revoke access. Resource Payment proof bytes and file metadata (Online server action or prepared-device upload endpoint): Authenticated business ID + UUID paymentId + sha256(file bytes) + safeObjectName(fileId, original name) -> payment-proofs bucket; upload then second authorization/transaction link. Effective: payment-proofs/{businessId}/payments/{paymentId}/{sha256}/{fileId}-{normalizedName}; name normalized to ASCII safe characters, <=96 original-name characters; <=3,500,000 bytes; JPEG/PNG/WebP/PDF signature checks. Recipients: Supabase private bucket; files/payments tables; audit metadata stores object path. Retry may download bytes server-side; orphan objects retained. Control: Active POS employee/current shift assignment; eligible non-cash payment; prepared-device ownership if reserved; business-scoped reads, file signature/size/type, upsert=false, digest retry verification, transaction linking. Reads additionally use SQL Storage policies. Resource Prepared-device identity and ownership (Online preparation then offline/reconnect, production versus development cookie setting): Server generates 32 random bytes in miniros-installation cookie -> SHA256 deviceId. Separate browser IndexedDB meta.storageInstallationId UUID -> x-miniros-storage header -> snapshot binding. Effective: Cookie miniros-installation: HttpOnly, SameSite=strict, path=/, maxAge=365 days, Secure only when NODE_ENV=production; database stores hash. Storage UUID stored in miniros-prepared-shifts/meta. Recipients: Cookie secret browser cookie jar/server; hash and storage UUID in offline_shift_sessions and prepared response; storage UUID available to same-origin browser JS. Control: Same-origin POST check; authentication/POS/assignment; comparisons of user, business, device hash, storage UUID, shift/session/snapshot IDs; row locks and one-owner partial unique index. No hardware attestation or isolation from a caller controlling the same browser principal.
